newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed firmer, aided by further strength in the U.S. market, but dealers said yields at the long end would probably not fall much further now.
"We'll probably see German 10-year yields fall just below six percent this year, so there's a little bit more upside, but not very much," said one dealer.
The Dutch January 2006 benchmark gained over 20 cents to 100.83/91 for a bid yield of 5.88 percent, a level last seen in January of this year.
But it underperformed the April 2006 German bund slightly, with the yield spread narrowing to -14 basis points from -16.
"It's beginning to look very toppy and overdone to me," said one dealer.
He said the Dutch market might see some profit-taking on Thursday, when Germany celebrates the unity day holiday, ahead of U.S. September payrolls data at 1230 GMT on Friday.
Dealers said that at some point the Dutch and German yield curves should start to flatten, with yields at the short end rising towards those on longer-dated paper.
"We've all been saying that for a long time now and it remains true, but nobody can say exactly when it will happen," said one dealer.

Dealers said that with Dutch government bonds becoming fairly scarce due to a sharp drop in borrowing needs, domestic investors were increasingly looking towards other guilder issuers as long as they offered an attractive yield premium.
One dealer said NIB's 125 million guilder Dec 2001 bond, with a spread of 14 basis points above government paper failed this test, describing the spread as "hilarious".
On the other hand, the 500 million guilder second tranche of ING's Feb 2006 bond offered a fairly generous 50 basis points over equivalent government paper, he said.
